title: Reviewing Need for SG Arrival Card for Returning Singaporeans and Residents
what_it_is: Reviewing Need for SG Arrival Card for Returning Singaporeans and Residents

sections.label: SG Arrival Card disease control
sections.summary: MOH implemented the digital SG Arrival Card so all travellers submit a health declaration to guard against importing diseases like Yellow Fever, MERS and Ebola.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the course of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Ministry of Health (MOH) reviewed our need for data collection at the borders and we decided to implement the digital SG Arrival Card system for purposes of disease control.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Specifically, we want to guard against importing infectious diseases of concern, such as Yellow Fever, Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) and Ebola.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: First, previously, only foreigners are required to submit health information on a physical card.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Now, all travellers are required to submit a health declaration because all travellers are subject to the risk of infectious diseases – not just the foreign travellers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Third, the information required has been streamlined and simplified to only three questions to ascertain the risk of a traveller being infected with the current diseases of concern.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Travellers at risk of Yellow Fever infection and do not have a valid relevant vaccination certificate are assessed and may be quarantined to protect against the risk of importation of Yellow Fever in Singapore.

sections.label: Permanent border health declaration feature
sections.summary: Travellers suspected of infection may be referred for assessment and isolation, and MOH deems the health declaration a permanent feature to keep diseases from becoming endemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Travelers suspected of being infected can be referred for further medical assessment and isolation if necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: These are dynamic information, based on their recent travel history and how they feel, and therefore, not captured in existing Government systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Meaning, if we were to stand down and then we need to re-activate it again, can the Ministry do it in a very expeditious way?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We reviewed this and we deemed this as a permanent feature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Yellow Fever, MERS – they have all become endemic diseases in their parts of the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We do not want them to become endemic diseases in our part of the world, which therefore means that this is quite a permanent feature, that as of now, we feel is necessary, to prevent such diseases from coming into Singapore.
